### Course Descriptions

1. **0401239 The Islamic Morals** (3 Credit Hours)  
   This course touches on the theoretical aspect in terms of: the definition of morality, its significance and whether it is acquired or not. Topics include obligation, responsibility, reward, intention, and motives. It also addresses practical aspects concerning individual, family, and social levels such as loyalty, honesty, sincerity, humbleness, mercy, filial piety, and good relations with relatives, cooperation, excellence, beneficence, and forgiveness, etc.

2. **0402204 Education in Islam** (3 Credit Hours)  
   The course aims at defining educational concepts and terms, and the relationship between Islam and education. It differentiates between Islamic education and other types of contemporary education concerning objectives, properties, and philosophy, and explores the sources and methods of Islamic education, as well as characteristics of an effective educator.

3. **0402232 Governance System in Islam** (3 Credit Hours)  
   This course explains the concept of the state, its modern pillars, and individuals liable to be consulted, as well as loyalty, election processes, constitutional reform, local state policies, legislative policies, authority styles, state restrictions, and constitutional punishment regarding rulers.

4. **0402262 The Legal Rulings and Indications** (3 Credit Hours)  
   This course highlights the rules of Fiqh, focusing on the effects of legal rules, indications (both obvious and obscure words), and their implications. Topics include the text and concept, general and special indications.

5. **0402324 The Islamic Economy** (3 Credit Hours)  
   This course deals with the jurisprudence of the Islamic economy, covering its importance, objectives, and properties. It also addresses economic problems, relevant ideologies (mathhab), property limits, property duties, and the financial system in Islam and its resources.
